name: Loch Lomond & the Trossachs
tagline: Scotland's first national park, an accessible first taste of the Highlands within easy reach of Glasgow.
highlight: Watching morning mist lift slowly off Loch Lomond from the pier at Luss, the Highland hills just beginning to catch the first light.
shortDescription: Scotland's first national park, home to Loch Lomond, Ben Lomond and the wooded hills of the Trossachs, an easy first taste of the Highlands from Glasgow.
metaDescription: A Loch Lomond and the Trossachs travel guide: Ben Lomond, Luss, Loch Katrine, food and how to plan a visit to Scotland's first national park.
knownFor: Loch Lomond, Ben Lomond, the Trossachs
goodFor: Hiking, scenic drives, an easy Highland taste

image.alt: Loch Lomond and the surrounding Highland hills

intro: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs is Scotland's first national park, and for good reason a favourite easy escape from Glasgow, offering a real first taste of Highland scenery within an hour's drive of the city.
Loch Lomond itself is Britain's largest lake by surface area, its southern shores gentle and accessible, its northern reaches narrowing into properly dramatic Highland terrain around Ben Lomond.

Most visitors combine a loch cruise or lakeside walk with time in the wooded Trossachs further east, where Loch Katrine's historic steamship and the area's inspired Sir Walter Scott's romantic writing about the Highlands.

whyVisit.intro: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs' case rests on offering real Highland scenery within easy reach of Glasgow.

points.title: It's Scotland's first national park
points.text: Established in 2002, protecting some of the country's most accessible Highland scenery.

points.title: Loch Lomond is Britain's largest lake by area
points.text: A real sense of scale, especially from the water on a loch cruise.

points.title: Ben Lomond is an achievable first Munro
points.text: One of the most accessible of Scotland's mountains over 3,000 feet for a first serious hike.

points.title: The Trossachs inspired Sir Walter Scott
points.text: His writing about the area helped popularise the wider romantic image of the Highlands.

points.title: It's an easy day trip or overnight from Glasgow
points.text: Under an hour's drive, making it accessible even on a short trip.

attractionsIntro: The park's essential sights combine Loch Lomond's accessible scale with the Trossachs' more intimate, wooded scenery.

attractions.name: Loch Lomond

image.alt: Loch Lomond, Britain's largest lake by surface area

attractions.text: Britain's largest lake by surface area, its southern shores gentle and its northern reaches narrowing into dramatic Highland terrain.
attractions.tip: The loch's character changes dramatically from south to north — see both if time allows.

attractions.name: Ben Lomond
attractions.text: One of Scotland's most accessible Munros, a mountain over 3,000 feet, with sweeping views over the loch from the summit.
attractions.tip: The standard route takes four to six hours round trip and needs no technical climbing.

attractions.name: Luss village

image.alt: The village of Luss on the shore of Loch Lomond

attractions.text: One of Scotland's prettiest lochside villages, its stone cottages and pier a popular, easy stop on the loch's western shore.
attractions.tip: Arrive early or late to avoid the busiest midday tour bus crowds.

attractions.name: Loch Katrine

image.alt: Loch Katrine in the heart of the Trossachs

attractions.text: The scenic heart of the Trossachs, a loch that helped inspire Sir Walter Scott's romantic writing about the Highlands.
attractions.tip: The surrounding forest offers excellent, easy cycling and walking trails.

attractions.name: The SS Sir Walter Scott

image.file: File:SS Sir Walter Scott At Trossachs Pier - geograph.org.uk - 4431047.jpg
image.alt: The SS Sir Walter Scott steamship on Loch Katrine

attractions.text: A historic Victorian steamship, still carrying passengers across Loch Katrine over a century after entering service.
attractions.tip: Book ahead in summer — it's one of the Trossachs' most popular attractions.

attractions.name: The Trossachs

image.alt: The wooded hills of the Trossachs at sunset

attractions.text: A more intimate, wooded landscape than Loch Lomond itself, often called 'the Highlands in miniature.'
attractions.tip: A rewarding scenic drive, best taken slowly with several stops.

attractions.name: Loch Lomond near Tarbet

image.alt: Loch Lomond near the village of Tarbet

attractions.text: Where the loch begins to narrow and turn properly Highland in character, a striking contrast to its wider southern reaches.
attractions.tip: A good stop for photos looking north toward the narrower, more dramatic upper loch.

thingsToDoIntro: The park rewards combining time on the water with a proper walk or hike.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise Loch Lomond

image.alt: A cruise boat on Loch Lomond

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to appreciate the loch's real scale, with regular sailings departing from Balloch and Luss.
thingsToDo.tip: A shorter cruise from Luss covers some of the loch's most scenic stretches.

thingsToDo.title: Hike Ben Lomond

image.file: File:North ridge of Ben Lomond - geograph.org.uk - 3231298.jpg
image.alt: Hiking the ridge of Ben Lomond

thingsToDo.text: An achievable first Munro for many visitors, rewarded with sweeping summit views over the loch.
thingsToDo.tip: Start early and check the weather — conditions change quickly at altitude even here.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Luss village
thingsToDo.text: An easy, pretty stop, strolling stone cottages and a short pier out onto the loch itself.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine with a coffee stop at one of the village's small cafés.

thingsToDo.title: Sail Loch Katrine on the SS Sir Walter Scott

image.file: File:SS Sir Walter Scott at Trossachs Pier - geograph.org.uk - 6857558.jpg
image.alt: Boarding the SS Sir Walter Scott on Loch Katrine

thingsToDo.text: A memorable way to see the Trossachs, a slow cruise aboard a working Victorian steamship.
thingsToDo.tip: Book ahead in peak summer, when sailings can sell out.

thingsToDo.title: Drive through the Trossachs

image.alt: A scenic drive through the Trossachs

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding, unhurried drive through wooded hills often described as 'the Highlands in miniature.'
thingsToDo.tip: Stop often — the scenery here rewards a slow pace more than covering distance.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph Ellen's Isle on Loch Katrine

image.file: File:Ellen's Isle, Loch Katrine, Trossachs, Scotland-LCCN2002695066.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A scenic small island, named for the heroine of Sir Walter Scott's poem set on the loch.
thingsToDo.tip: Best viewed from the SS Sir Walter Scott's regular cruise route.

accommodation.intro: Luss and Balloch serve as the park's main bases, both well set up for day trips from Glasgow.

areas.name: Luss
areas.bestFor: Being picturesque and central to the loch's western shore
areas.text: A small, pretty base with easy access to loch cruises and Ben Lomond.

areas.name: Balloch
areas.bestFor: A practical gateway town with more amenities
areas.text: The park's southern entry point, well connected by train to Glasgow.

options.text: Direct from Glasgow, taking under an hour.
options.detail: One of the easiest national park connections by public transport in Scotland.

options.text: A popular no-driving option from Glasgow or Edinburgh.
options.detail: Widely available, often combined with Stirling or the wider Highlands.

options.detail: Roads within the park are generally well maintained and scenic.

bestTime.headline: May to September for the best weather, though the park works well year-round
bestTime.summary: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs are visitable in any season, though hiking and cruising are easiest in the warmer months.

seasons.text: Mild weather and thinner crowds than midsummer.
The warmest and busiest season, with the best conditions for Ben Lomond.
Beautiful, with the Trossachs' forest turning colour.
Short days and frequent rain, though atmospheric, with far fewer visitors.

bestTime.avoid: Attempting Ben Lomond in poor visibility or high wind — a real hazard even on this relatively accessible mountain.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Loch Lomond and Trossachs visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book SS Sir Walter Scott sailings ahead in peak summer.
Start early for Ben Lomond — the trailhead car park fills fast on fine days.
Check weather conditions before any higher-altitude hike.
Pack a proper waterproof layer regardless of season.
Visit Luss early or late to avoid the busiest midday tour bus crowds.
Consider the train to Balloch if visiting without a car.

faq.q: How many days do you need at Loch Lomond and the Trossachs?
faq.a: One to two days covers Luss, a loch cruise and the Trossachs comfortably.

faq.q: Can you visit as a day trip from Glasgow?
faq.a: Yes, easily — Balloch is under an hour away by train, making it one of Scotland's most accessible national parks.

faq.q: Is Ben Lomond difficult to climb?
faq.a: Moderate — it's one of the more accessible Munros, taking four to six hours round trip without requiring technical climbing skill.

faq.q: What is Loch Lomond known for?
faq.a: Being Britain's largest lake by surface area, and for inspiring the well-known folk song of the same name.

faq.q: Is the SS Sir Walter Scott worth it?
faq.a: Yes — it's a historic working Victorian steamship, and a memorable, relaxed way to see Loch Katrine.

faq.q: How far is Loch Lomond from Glasgow?
faq.a: Very close, under an hour's drive or train ride, making it an easy day trip or short overnight from the city.
